brief: desktop app for supervising AI coding agents

defects.what: Pending approval (blocking, constant) sits below the fold; only a small badge shows at load
Solid accent 'New chat' is the loudest element, louder than Approve; accent reused for logo, send, avatar, selection
About nine header icon buttons, mostly rare and duplicated in More; seven sidebar nav items ahead of the chat list
defects.expectNote: too-many-peers mapped 2026-11-19 after the rule was written

defects.what: Approve/Deny/Always allow are ordinary small buttons with no shortcuts; Always allow sits right next to Approve
'Always allow' grants a standing rule beside one-time Approve with no confirmation; scope text does not cover the chained command
Chat status by small low-contrast dot colour alone; waiting chats not grouped above idle
Group headers, footnote, sub-lines and key chip are small and low contrast
On phone the approval card is even further below the fold; send button wraps to its own row
On phone the 'waiting for you' badge is hidden, title truncated, goal bar wraps awkwardly
'Full auto' is one click away in a plain list with no warning or confirmation
Permission mode is a tiny muted pill with an unexplained coloured dot; menu offset hard-coded on phone
Model, effort and permission are three near-identical peer pills; effort loses its label on phone
'Stop agent' sits under 'Export transcript' with only red text, no separator or confirmation
defects.expectNote: destructive-unseparated mapped 2026-11-19 after the rule was written

defects.what: Delete removes a chat immediately with no confirmation or undo; kebab invisible until hover
Toggles, select and read-only usage stats in one list with identical separators
Focus lands on the X with a heavy ring; both X and Cancel; no pending-change state
defects.note: The focus-ring part may come from the harness: surfaces are opened with a scripted click, and Chrome shows focus rings when there was no real pointer input.

defects.what: Toast covers the composer's effort and permission controls and duplicates in-button feedback

reviewer: Claude Sonnet, blind review of screenshots and source (never saw the rule list)
